summary: Inconsistent SSO session TTL after Okta group merge prevents access to legacy deploy tool
description: Issue summary: Several engineers lost interactive access to the legacy deploy console immediately after an Okta group consolidation (security:devops -> securityops). Impact: blocked deploys for a team of ~8 engineers, intermittent CI failures tied to the same service account. Symptoms surfaced as immediate login followed by forced logout (5-10s) or access denied errors when opening the deploy UI. This appears limited to the legacy console and service catalog UI while modern Redwood Console and API access remain functional for affected users.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Okta admin, merge group 'security:devops' into 'securityops' (SCIM group update simulated in staging).
2) User logs into console via SSO; initial session established successfully (SSO assertion accepted).
3) Within 5-15 seconds, user is logged out or receives 'Access denied: RBAC role not found' when accessing legacy deploy endpoints.
4) Reverting to original group membership (re-adding user to old group) restores stable access after a login cycle.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:04Z auth: received SAML assertion for user m.lee@redwood.com; session_expires_in=3600
2026-03-10T14:12:10Z rbac: evaluated roles for user m.lee@redwood.com; roles resolved=[deploy-read,ci-runner]
2026-03-10T14:12:14Z console-legacy: authorization failed for user m.lee@redwood.com: role mapping missing -> 403
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SCIM group merge triggered an Okta attribute change that injected a short session TTL claim into SAML/OIDC assertions for affected users.
Checked Okta system logs: group merge event (id: okta-event-20260310-991) shows SCIM delta applied; no immediate errors from Okta side.

Compared SAML assertions for affected vs unaffected users: affected assertions include an unexpected 'session_expires_in' claim set to 30 (seconds) in addition to standard 'exp' claim. Unaffected users have normal 3600s claim.

Auth middleware (token intake service) logs show a code path that honors 'session_expires_in' when present; legacy console session manager previously used a different TTL source and both systems are now conflicting after a config flag flip during last week's rollout.
Relevant config flip: PR https://github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/4387 enabled honoring TTL claims from identity provider for all clients (intended for modern console only).
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed users were instantly kicked out while trying to approve a canary deploy. Affected users show rapid re-login loops.

Alejandro Ruiz (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally by simulating SCIM merge in staging and saw 30s TTL claim. Escalating to Auth eng for quick revert or selective ignore of provider TTL for legacy console.
Priya Nair (Auth Eng) 2026-03-11: Confirmed PR 4387 added global env var HONOR_IDP_TTL=true. Proposing to scope this to clients in CLIENT_ALLOW_IDP_TTL list to avoid breaking legacy session managers.
SRE oncall 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation applied — added legacy-console to CLIENT_ALLOW_IDP_TTL=false and restarted auth-intake pods. Monitoring for recurrence.
Maya Chen 2026-03-12: Partial rollback restored access for 6 of 8 users; two users still seeing 403 due to cached RBAC mapping; advised to clear sessions and re-login.
Alejandro Ruiz 2026-03-13: Follow-up: creating patch to auth-service to default to provider TTL only if > 300s. Will schedule canary deploy to staging first.
resolution: Mitigation: SRE applied a service-level override to ignore provider TTL for legacy-console clients (temporary) on 2026-03-12.
Permanent fix: Auth-service patch to treat IDP-supplied TTL as advisory; only accept if >= 300s or client explicitly opted in. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/4410.
Rollout notes: will canary to staging on 2026-03-14, then prod canary (10%) on 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-16 pending green metrics.
Follow-ups: runbook update to include 'honor_idp_ttl' flag behavior, postmortem to review change control for global auth flags.
Status: In Progress — mitigation successful; permanent fix under code review.
